```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Annotation Breakpoint asks a conditional sensitivity question: under a fixed
set of allowed cell labels, constraints, and an analysis specification, how
many label changes are sufficient to move a registered donor-level expression
effect to its decision boundary? A returned witness describes sensitivity to
the declared inputs. It does not identify the biologically correct labels.

## Read and validate an input

The installed `exact_toy` directory contains the six ordinary input tables.
The reader is also used by the command-line interface.

```{r validate}
library(AnnotationBreakpoint)

example_dir <- system.file(
  "extdata", "examples", "exact_toy",
  package = "AnnotationBreakpoint"
)
read_inputs <- getFromNamespace(
  "read_input_directory", "AnnotationBreakpoint"
)
inputs <- read_inputs(example_dir)

validation <- do.call(
  validate_inputs,
  inputs[c(
    "counts", "cells", "specimens", "allowed_labels",
    "claim", "constraints", "analysis_spec"
  )]
)
stopifnot(validation$ok)
validation$status
```

For the authoritative edgeR backend, pass the frozen analysis specification
and leave `runtime_policy = "strict"`, the default. Strict mode requires the
recorded R and edgeR versions exactly. When only the patch version differs,
`runtime_policy = "compatible"` requests a capability-checked run:

```{r compatible-policy, eval=FALSE}
validation <- validate_inputs(
  counts, cells, specimens, allowed_labels, claim, constraints,
  analysis_spec = analysis_spec,
  runtime_policy = "compatible"
)
```

Compatible mode does not relax the analysis specification. It rejects major
or minor version differences and an edgeR installation without the required
quasi-likelihood arguments. Results, cache identity, and replay records retain
the expected and observed runtime versions and the selected policy.

## Run the default search

`proxy_prefix` ranks permitted single-cell changes once at the observed labels
and fully refits the available cumulative prefixes at fixed sizes. An
inadmissible exact prefix is recorded and skipped without repair. The smallest
evaluated crossing is independently replayed before it is reported.

```{r proxy-prefix}
search <- search_breakpoint(
  validation,
  method = "proxy_prefix",
  max_fits = 32,
  seed = 82901L
)
c(
  status = search$status,
  best_verified_cost = search$best_verified_cost
)
```

A `verified_counterexample` is an upper bound on breakpoint cost. A
`no_counterexample_found` result remains unresolved because the practical
route does not rule out untested assignments.

The same frozen-ranking method can evaluate a caller-supplied prefix schedule:

```{r custom-prefixes, eval=FALSE}
custom_search <- search_breakpoint(
  validation,
  method = "proxy_prefix",
  max_fits = 32,
  seed = 82901L,
  prefix_sizes = c(1L, 3L, 6L, 12L)
)
```

`prefix_sizes` must be a unique, strictly increasing vector of positive
integers. It selects exact prefixes from the same ranking; it does not trigger
reranking or constraint repair. The selected schedule is recorded in result
identity and the prefix log. Leaving it `NULL` uses
`c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128)`. The CLI equivalent is
`--prefix-sizes 1,3,6,12`.

The requested schedule is available as
`custom_search$proxy_prefix$registered_prefix_sizes`; the subset that fits the
declared domain is `custom_search$proxy_prefix$available_prefix_sizes`.

## Use exact enumeration for a small domain

Exact enumeration is the one supported alternative. It is limited to at most
12 ambiguous cells and 4,096 allowed assignments. An `exact_minimum` rules out
every cheaper feasible assignment; `exhaustively_stable` means every feasible
assignment fitted successfully and none crossed the threshold.

```{r exact}
exact <- enumerate_breakpoint(validation)
c(
  status = exact$status,
  exact_minimum_cost = exact$exact_minimum_cost
)
```

## Replay and render

Replay recomputes hashes, constraints, cost, assignment identity, and fitted
effects from the immutable inputs. A report can be rendered only from a
successful verification tied to the same result.

```{r replay}
verification <- verify_witness(validation, exact)
stopifnot(verification$ok)

output_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "annotation-breakpoint-example")
artifacts <- render_report(
  exact,
  verification,
  output_dir,
  run_metadata = list(example = "exact_toy", interface = "R")
)
basename(artifacts$paths)
```

The report directory contains JSON and TSV records plus a readable Markdown
summary. If the original fit is unavailable, its structured failure reason,
backend error, warnings, and expected/observed runtime versions remain in the
result artifacts. These fields distinguish a failed or mismatched analysis
from a valid no-hit.

The repository's [evidence index](https://github.com/yhengaa/AnnotationBreakpoint/blob/main/reports/PUBLICATION/README.md)
preserves the saved positive examples together with negative and inconclusive
evaluation results.
